name: Sambe
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source.
catalog_citation: Blench, Roger. 2015. Final Records of the Sambe Language of Central Nigeria: Phonology, Noun Morphology, and Wordlist. Language Documentation & Conservation 9: 192-228.http://hdl.handle.net/10125/24641(publisher PDF, LD&C/ScholarSpace; CC BY-NC 4.0)
catalog_locator: §3.3 Tones, p. 199; caveat at §3 Phonology, p. 194; saved
catalog_quote: 3.3 TONES. Sambe was transcribed with three level tones and a rising and falling tone. These are marked as follows High ˊ Mid Unmarked Low ˋ Falling ˆ Rising ˇ Vowels without tones marked are therefore mid. Initial nasals, such as m- may or may not be tone-bearing. The tone, which is always low, is marked where it was heard. There was some variation in tone between the two sessions, so the tones cannot be considered wholly reliable. [p. 199] ... 3. PHONOLOGY. The phonology of Sambe is based on the two wordlists and should therefore be regarded as tentative. In particular the informants’ tone was somewhat unstable and no conclusions should be drawn from the tone, which was marked as heard. [p. 194]
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.rule_in_words: Sambe is described as a tone language with three level tones (high, mid, low) plus rising and falling contours; the source says nothing at all about word stress or accent, so no stress placement rule can be extracted.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. The author warns (p. 194) that 'the informants' tone was somewhat unstable and no conclusions should be drawn from the tone, which was marked as heard'; data were written by ear without a recorder from two to six very aged speakers in 2001 and 2005.
new_statements.domain_note: Wordlist citation forms only (isolated lexical items); no phrase-level or intonational description.
new_statements.identity_note: The source describes Sambe [xab] = samb1307 exactly: the single village of Sambe (Kaduna State, near Agameti on the Fadan Karshe–Wamba road), closest relative Hasha, Alumic subgroup of Plateau. No dialects; Sambe had earlier been misfiled as a dialect of Ninzo (ninz1244) in Ethnologue, but Blench states it is not a Ninzo dialect. Language presumed extinct after 2005 (two speakers aged ~90 and ~85).

new_statements.relation_note: Same author, earlier state of the same description as the catalogued Blench 2015 LD&C statement: three level tones + rising + falling, no stress statement. The 2006/2010 draft states the tone inventory more flatly ('Sambe has three tone levels..') where the 2015 version hedges ('was transcribed with.. cannot be sure these tones were phonemic'). No new placement information. How opened: live rogerblench.info still serves a SiteGround sg-captcha proof-of-work challenge (HTTP 202) by automated download with a browser User-Agent and --max-time 300 (not solved); the current /Plateau/Sambe/ directory is not in the the Internet Archive (web/2/ -> 404); a the Internet Archive's index domain search…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Sambe is described as a tone language with three level tones plus a rising and a falling (contour) tone; the draft says nothing about word stress, accent or prominence anywhere in the recovered text (sections 1-4 and wordlist items 1 to c. 370). The phonology is explicitly flagged as tentative (rapid observations, two very aged last speakers).
new_statements.exceptions: none; the only caveat is that the whole phonology is tentative. The later 2015 pre-print of the same material (also saved, section 3.3 p. 6) adds that 'The articulation of the informants was simply no longer sufficiently precise to be sure that these tones were phonemic.'
new_statements.identity_note: Both documents describe the same variety: Sambe of Sambe village (c. 10 km west of Agamati, Fadan Karshe-Wamba road, Kaduna State), elicited 2001 and 2005 from the last two to six very aged speakers; Blench states it is not a dialect of Ninzo and that its closest relative is Hasha (Yashi). The language is now presumed extinct, so no further primary data is expected.
